sources.title: UNESCO, Pyu Ancient Cities
sources.note: Direct institutional description: Halin, Beikthano and Sri Ksetra; broad 200 BCE to 900 CE nomination chronology, urban water management, craft and religious continuity. No single kingdom inferred.

sources.title: Stargardt and colleagues, Early urban archaeology in Southeast Asia: the first evidence for a Pyu habitation site at Sri Ksetra, Myanmar
sources.note: Full excavation report read. January/February 2015 Yahanda HMA59 test pits. Work floors mid-fifth to late-seventh and probably eighth century; lower house pre-fifth century. No invented event-year midpoints or proved kinship.

sources.title: Bob Hudson and Terry Lustig, Communities of the past: A new view of the old walls and hydraulic system at Sriksetra, Myanmar (2008)
sources.note: Author-deposited full text read, Journal of Southeast Asian Studies 39(2), 269 to 296, DOI 10.1017/S0022463408000210. Printed pages 278 to 279 political transition/votive tablets; 283 to 284 drainage. Differing published enclosed-area measurements excluded.

sources.title: U Aung Myint and Elizabeth Moore, Finger-marked designs on ancient bricks in Myanmar (1991)
sources.note: Direct 22-page PDF, printed page 83/PDF page 3: making grooves, rice chaff and the Kyoto rice study. Shared Mon/Pyu craft, not exclusive ethnic fingerprint.

sources.title: British Museum, Pyu silver coin, 1996,0103.52
sources.note: Direct collection record, circa sixth century, 20 mm, 2.28 g, rising sun and srivatsa. Donated in 1996; no excavated findspot established.

sources.title: Andrew Harris and colleagues, Currents of currency (2025)
sources.note: Direct full article, DOI 10.15184/aqy.2025.77. Dataset collected 1022 coins but analytical sample 245 full-unit coins; these are not interchangeable counts. Die-match method and Bangladesh/Oc Eo link directly read.

sources.title: Tilman Frasch, Pyu urns, Indian calendars, and Myanmar culture (2024)
sources.note: Direct paper, introduction and Payagyi urns section. Royal attribution probable, calendar and name-order debated; no definitive chronological king list copied.

sources.title: Griffiths, Miyake and Wheatley, Stone pillar from Myazedi pagoda, Myinkaba, Pagan (A), DHARMA
sources.note: Direct scholarly edition: Pyu face line 1 siri and line 4 saḥ. Summary translation records shrine and three villages of enslaved workers. Grouped conservatively with Miyake main paper and appendix.

sources.title: Marc Miyake, A new study of the Pyu face of the Kubyaukgyi (Myazedi) inscription: glossary and apparatus
sources.note: Original open appendix downloaded via file 47737858, 100 PDF pages. Printed page 66/PDF index 65 saḥ = son; printed page 67/PDF index 66 siri = opening glory. Main study DOI 10.1163/19606028-bja10045 abstract dates pillars circa 1112 and describes RTI photography; UNESCO uses 1113. Public date early twelfth century.

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Myazedi quadrilingual stone inscription nomination
sources.note: Direct ten-page nomination. Printed pages 7 to 8: Pagan setting, temple lighting, gold Buddha for sick father, endowed villages with enslaved workers. Romantic assertions about private emotions and disputed oldest-language claims omitted.

proposedOverrides.name: Pyu heritage in the Pagan period
proposedOverrides.summary: A later atlas label for the Pyu region, read through cultural and linguistic survival rather than separate sovereignty.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One deliberately diachronic cultural-identity card, not an alias claiming unchanged statehood. Exact shared geometry verified in three snapshots; Pyu-language continuity and old urban sites make the cultural subject compatible. Titles and public overview correct the imported singular state implication. Pagan and Bagan records remain separate.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: pyu-state 800 to 900; pyu-state-1100 1100 to 1200 and 1200 to 1279. No polygon between 900 and 1100 is filled by this association. The second record is Pagan-period regional context, not independently demonstrated Pyu sovereignty. Early domestic evidence is overtly pre-800, and Myazedi later evidence is explicitly twelfth century.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: All three imported features share bbox 93.96633966339664,18.58682674176731 to 96.6987669876699,22.73148585025416. Point checks include Sri Ksetra, Beikthano, Halin, Bagan and Mandalay; omit Yangon. Broad outline is not a surveyed political boundary. See geometry-checks.json and equality check.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: DHARMA INSPYU00007 line 1 siri; line 4 saḥ. Miyake appendix printed page 67 glosses siri as Glory, a Pali borrowing; page 66 glosses saḥ as son. Main study circa1112, UNESCO1113: public early twelfth century. Only scholarly transliteration is rendered, no invented modern Burmese substitution.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No universal school, family structure, cure, sewer or toilet claim. Rice chaff is plant evidence, not complete diet. Buried house does not prove kinship. Inscribed urn royal attribution/calendar unresolved. Nanzhao raid narratives and blanket832 destruction not used. Contradictory measured enclosed areas18.57 versus14.3 square kilometers omitted rather than reconciled speculatively.
